name: Coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2)
headline: diameter
subtitle: SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19
description: SARS-CoV-2 is the coronavirus behind the COVID-19 pandemic. Under the electron microscope its particles look roughly round, studded with spike proteins that give the family its crown-like appearance. Early imaging measured the particles at about 60 to 140 nm across, and later cryo-electron studies of Omicron sublineages found average diameters of about 75 to 82 nm.

measures.note: Range from early electron-microscope observations of the virion

measures.label: Mean diameter (Omicron BA.1 to BA.2)
measures.note: Mean diameters from cryo-electron tomography: BA.1 75.0 +/- 7.9 nm, BA.2 81.5 +/- 6.6 nm

measures.label: Spike protein diameter
measures.note: Width of the spike proteins projecting from the envelope

facts.text: Cryo-electron tomography counted on average about 23 pre-fusion spikes on each Omicron BA.1 particle and about 35 on each BA.2 particle, compared with about 26 reported for the original virus.
The Omicron BA.1 and BA.2 particles were found to be similar in size to the original (wild-type) virus grown in the same cells.

caveats: No CDC, NIH or NIAID web page stating the particle size could be fetched (NIAID returned 403 and PubMed returned a CAPTCHA), so sizes come from peer-reviewed papers hosted on NIH's PubMed Central.
Particles are pleomorphic (not perfectly round), and measured size depends on variant, preparation and imaging method.
No sourced mass or volume was found.
